haiku-low.q1: 02:00 UTC scheduler trigger starts it. It extracts replica orders with updated_at after HWM minus 2 hours, including soft-deleted rows.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports can hold transactions open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is set at write time. Visibility lags up to 90 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: The edit bumps updated_at past the HWM, so a later nightly extract re-reads the row and the MERGE applies it, since newer updated_at wins.
haiku-low.q4: It sets deleted_at, which also bumps updated_at. The warehouse keeps the row and sets is_deleted = true; rows are never removed.
haiku-low.q5: Attempt fails: run_log marked failed, retry after 15 minutes with new run_id and same HWM, max 3 attempts. Third failure pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed state, not a partial load. A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares per-creation-day counts and checksums over 30 days, then re-extracts and upserts mismatched days.
haiku-low.q8: The dedupe keeps the latest updated_at per order_id within a run, and MERGE updates only when incoming updated_at is greater than the stored one.
haiku-low.q9: In etl.control's high_water_mark column (timestamptz, one row per pipeline). It is set to GREATEST of HWM and max staged updated_at, inside the commit transaction.
haiku-low.q10: A single warehouse transaction: merge, HWM advance and committed status commit together or roll back; dashboards see old or finished data.
haiku-low.q11: Retry first deletes all leftover staged rows from earlier failed attempts. It extracts again from the same HWM minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: Every row of each mismatched day (by created_at) is re-read from the replica and upserted, newer wins. The HWM is not touched.

sonnet.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler trigger starts attempt 1. It extracts all orders (including soft-deleted) from the Postgres read replica with updated_at > HWM minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports can hold a transaction open up to 90 minutes and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit time, so the row becomes visible on the replica up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so a later nightly extract (updated_at > HWM-2h) picks it up, stages it, and the commit step MERGEs it into dw.orders as an update because the incoming updated_at is greater.
sonnet.q4: The app only sets deleted_at (which also bumps updated_at). The nightly extract includes it, and the warehouse updates the row in place with is_deleted = true; it is never removed.
sonnet.q5: The commit rolls back (dw.orders and HWM unchanged), run_log is marked failed. If fewer than 3 attempts, wait 15 minutes and start a new attempt (new run_id, same HWM, full redo), at most twice. The third failure pages on-call, the run stays failed and HWM is not advanced.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the last committed state (not a partial one). A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts. The run and retries keep going.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares per-creation-day count and checksum between replica and warehouse for the last 30 days, re-extracts every row of mismatched days from the replica, and merges them (newer wins), assuming the replica has caught up.
sonnet.q8: The commit dedupes staged rows keeping the latest updated_at per order_id (ROW_NUMBER), and the MERGE updates a matched row only when s.updated_at > t.updated_at, so older or identical versions never overwrite newer ones.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl.control (high_water_mark, one row per pipeline). It is set to GREATEST of the current HWM and the max updated_at staged for the run (not wall clock), inside the commit transaction together with the merge and the committed status; skipped if staging is empty.
sonnet.q10: The commit step is a single warehouse transaction (dedupe, merge, HWM advance, committed status, staging delete), so dashboards see either old data or the finished night. Staging is read only by the commit step and dashboards never read it.
sonnet.q11: The next attempt first deletes all leftover staged rows from earlier failed attempts, then loads under its new run_id. The retry extracts the same window, since the HWM is unchanged (HWM minus 2 hours), a full redo.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads every row of each mismatched day from the replica (WHERE created_at falls on that day) into staging under a recon run_id. They are applied in one warehouse transaction covering all mismatched days using the same dedupe and MERGE (upsert, newer wins), and it writes recon_log and deletes staged rows. It does not touch the HWM.
